subject: Acme HealthSystems: Cloud channel listing - technical & procurement questionnaire

Subject: Cloud channel listing questionnaire - Acme RFI sections

Diego / Ben,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to Acme HealthSystems' channel listing questionnaire for AWS/Azure/GCP. Procurement sent over the initial packet and highlighted three sections we need to validate for listing:

- Vendor eligibility & ownership (legal/contracting)
- Technical integration & tenant isolation (deployment patterns for each cloud)
- Security & compliance (SOC 2, encryption, key management, data residency)

Can you confirm which artifacts you can provide and an estimated turnaround? There is an internal review meeting on 2025-08-20 and our procurement lead would like a consolidated response at least 3 business days before.

Attachments in their packet refer to: "Cloud_Channel_Listing_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx" (we have it available if you need). Also please indicate if any items require an NDA or PO before sharing.

Would appreciate an owner for each section so I can track internally.

Best,
Lara Chen
Sourcing Lead, Acme HealthSystems
Lara.Chen@acme-health.com

Acme HealthSystems — Strategic Sourcing

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:30:00 -0700

Diego / Grace — starting draft answers for procurement & contracting questions below. I pulled the basic pricing cadence and marketplace notes.

--- excerpt (procurement / pricing) ---
Q: Do you support metered billing on AWS Marketplace?
A: Yes. Redwood supports both SaaS metered billing (AWS Metering Service) and AMI/instance-based listings; we recommend SaaS-metered listings for most customers to preserve multi-tenant pricing controls. See attached pricing_matrix.csv for examples.

Q: Do you require PO or advance payment for cloud marketplace listings?
A: No for standard marketplace flow; enterprise customers may sign a commitment for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) under a separate seat/license agreement. PO/advance payment handled on a case-by-case basis.

--- end excerpt ---

Grace: need your confirmation on whether the Dedicated capacity contract language requires a separate SOW or if our standard terms suffice for Acme's procurement team. Also tagging Diego for the per-cloud listing notes where we call out tenant isolation.

Attachment: pricing_matrix.csv (csv)

Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud channel listing questionnaire - Acme RFI sections

Thanks — I pulled the compliance artifacts and made a short summary. Key points and required evidence for Acme's security team: 

- SOC 2 Type II: We can share the executive summary (attached: soc2-type2-summary.pdf). Full attestation available under NDA.
- Encryption at rest & in transit: We use TLS1.2+ for transport. At-rest encryption varies by deployment: for Hosted API we use cloud-provider-managed KMS; for Private deployment we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integration. Need to call out key rotation policy and KMS region mapping.
- Tenant isolation: For marketplace SaaS listings we run strong logical isolation (per-tenant namespaces, prefixes for KV caches). For Dedicated / Private offers we provide isolated GPU pools and VPC peering options. Will draft the architecture snippets per-cloud.
- Data residency & retention: We can commit to regional hosting within US/EU based on contract; retention policy configurable with retention/export APIs. Need Acme's expected retention period to fill exact numbers.
- Pen testing & audits: We provide annual penetration testing summaries and can furnish test scopes.

Notes for Ben: the Dedicated capacity offering does involve a separate SOW when there are on-prem or reserved GPU commitments. That SOW also includes acceptance tests and an SLA addendum; procurement typically expects it.

I uploaded the artifacts to the shared drive link below and redlined a few sections in the draft plan.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cExampleSharedDrive
Attachment: soc2-type2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance (interim)
Redwood Inference

Lara — attached is our consolidated RFI response for Acme (Redwood_RFI_Consolidated_Acme_20250815.pdf). Highlights: 

- We enumerated architecture patterns for AWS/Azure/GCP listing options and tenant isolation per-cloud (see section 2).
- Security artifacts: SOC 2 Type II executive summary included; full report available under NDA (Grace can route).
- KMS/HSM: support for cloud-managed KMS for Hosted; customer-managed CMKs and HSM integrations supported for Private/Dedicated.
- Commercial: marketplace metered flows supported; Dedicated capacity requires a separate SOW for reserved capacity and SLA addendum (Ben can provide template).

Action items / mutual action plan (short):
1) You to confirm desired retention period and whether Acme requires dedicated region hosting (US-only vs. US+EU).
2) Acme to advise if procurement requires the full SOC 2 report (we can provide under NDA).
3) Propose a 30-minute sync next week to walk the packet: Tue 2025-08-19 10:00am PT or Wed 2025-08-20 09:00am PT.

Attachments: Redwood_RFI_Consolidated_Acme_20250815.pdf (pdf)

If you'd prefer a shared Drive folder for ongoing artifact access I can move the files there; otherwise, confirm and we'll send a DocuSign request for the Dedicated SOW when you request reserved capacity.

Looking forward to the sync —
